help.intro: A crystal works only on its own family's ores: each section header lists them. Within a family, the type trades how much ore you keep against residue, the ore a rock loses that nobody gets.
help.a: Most ore from each rock. The full yield bonus with little or no extra residue. The default, and the pick when rocks are scarce or shared, like a fleet working one belt.
help.b: Most ore an hour. A's yield each cycle on a shorter cycle (10% shorter on Tech I, 20% on Tech II), but a higher residue chance, so each rock runs out sooner.
help.c: Clears rocks. A fraction of the yield, with a very high chance of heavy residue, so the rock empties fastest. For clearing a belt or site, not for profit.
help.tech2: Tech II A and B mine more than Tech I, and B II cycles faster still. C II mines even less than C I and clears faster still. Tech II needs more skill and costs more.
help.table: The table under each family shows this Fitting's own figures with that crystal loaded.

industry.materialPriceBasisTooltip: Which side of the hub's order book your materials are costed at. Sell orders is what you pay to buy them right now; buy orders is what they cost if you place orders and wait to be filled. breakdown.title: How this Build Plan is calculated
breakdown.intro: Live {{hub}} prices and this plan's own inputs. Every number below is the one the plan is using now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsSell: Materials: {{hub}} lowest sell — what you pay to buy them now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsBuy: Materials: {{hub}} highest buy — what they cost if you place orders and wait.
breakdown.pricesOre: Ore, ice and gas: priced as themselves. Refining is not modelled, so a plan that eats minerals prices minerals.
breakdown.pricesOwned: Owned units: 0 ISK. Ore you mined is free here — the plan does not charge what you could have sold it for.
breakdown.pricesBuilt: Built materials: their own recipe instead of a price — inputs plus total job cost, at every level you chose to build.
breakdown.pricesProduct: {{product}}: always {{hub}} lowest sell, whichever side the materials use.
breakdown.materials: Quantity after ME {{me}} waste (rounded once per job, not per run) × unit price. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.materialsReaction: Quantity × unit price. Reactions have no ME, so no waste is saved. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.jobFee: EIV is CCP's reference value for the materials at ME 0 — a yardstick, not what you pay. {{system}}'s index ({{index}}) scales it, SCC adds 4%, the structure owner adds tax.
breakdown.jobFeeFormula: EIV {{eiv}} → cost index fee {{costIndexFee}} + SCC 4% {{scc}} + facility tax {{facilityTax}} = {{total}}
breakdown.totalCostFormula: Total cost = materials {{materials}} + total job cost {{fee}} = {{total}}
breakdown.revenueTitle: Revenue, sales tax and broker fee
breakdown.revenueAssumption: Assumes it fills at today's lowest sell. Undercutting, price moves and time on the market are not modelled.
breakdown.fees: From your skills: Accounting {{accounting}} sets sales tax, Broker Relations {{broker}} sets broker fee. Standings toward the station owner: {{factionStanding}} faction, {{corpStanding}} corp.
breakdown.profitNet: Net = revenue − sales tax − broker fee − total cost. The default.
breakdown.profitGross: Gross = revenue − total cost. Ignores both market fees — only realistic if you never list it.
breakdown.profitIskPerHour: ISK/hour = profit ÷ build time ({{time}}). Slot time, not time to sell.
breakdown.breakEven: What one unit must list at to cover the whole job. Fees come out of the listed price, so it sits above cost per unit.
breakdown.breakEvenFloor: Broker fee has a 100 ISK per-order minimum. Under that, 100 ISK is used and the price re-solved.
breakdown.verdictAcquisition: Acquisition: is building {{product}} cheaper than buying it? Nothing is sold, so no tax and no broker fee.
breakdown.verdictSale: Sale profitability: does building then selling make money? That one pays both fees. Same hub price, different question.
breakdown.useOrSellBody: Owned units cost the plan nothing, so the profit above is what you make on top of stock you already hold. Build if that beats what the materials would fetch, sell if it does not.
breakdown.useOrSellBases: Sell now: fills standing buy orders — paid at once, sales tax only. Sell order: lists at the hub's sell price — more ISK, but broker fee (100 ISK minimum) and you wait.
breakdown.useOrSellUnpriced: No order on the chosen side means no verdict, rather than a total that quietly drops it.
breakdown.useOrSellScope: Only the owned units this job eats are valued. Surplus is out of scope, and a material set to Built counts as itself, not as the stock behind its recipe.

login.permissionsHint: Logging in lets it read your skills and training queue, wallet, assets, blueprints, industry jobs, mining ledger, market orders, contracts, mail, calendar, contacts, standings, clones and implants, planetary colonies, loyalty points, notifications, current location, your in-game fittings, and the player structures you can dock at — both their names and a search across them, which is how a build location is picked. EVE's consent screen lists the planetary scope as "manage your planetary installations" — Neocom Desk only reads that data and never writes to it. Corporation data (including your in-game corporation roles) and player-structure markets are separate grants, requested only if you open the pages that need them. Log in again after an update to pick up newly requested permissions. Want to share less from the start? Use Log in with custom permissions, next to the Log in button, to choose exactly what you grant.
login.writeExceptions: It also asks for five permissions that write, and uses each only when you act: opening a mail in this app also marks it read in EVE, so it won't show as unread again after a refresh; responding Accept, Decline, or Tentative to a calendar invite here also sends that response to EVE; replying to or forwarding a mail you write here sends it through your EVE account, the same as sending it from the game client; saving a Fitting to EVE creates or replaces your in-game fitting there, the same as fitting it in the client; and setting a route's waypoints in game replaces your autopilot waypoints in the EVE client. Nothing else in the app writes to EVE.
login.eyebrow: Free · Open source · Runs on your device
login.heading: Answers, not API dumps.
login.answersHeading: The questions it exists to answer
login.answersLead: Each of these is a page you open after logging in, with the number you would have worked out by hand already worked out.

attention.question: Which character needs my attention?
attention.answer: The character list shows every pilot’s training queue at a glance: training, paused, ending soon or sitting idle. Alerts gathers what fired for every character on this device, not just the one you are looking at: skills finished, jobs ready to deliver, colonies stopped, orders undercut, mail waiting. Open a character and its board leads with the nearest deadline.

orders.question: Which of my orders is quietly losing ISK?
orders.answer: Open Orders is a worklist, not a list. Every order is filed under the worst thing wrong with it — undercut at your station, system or region, sitting under the price where relisting stops paying, or about to expire — worst first, across every character you fly. Open one and it prices the ways out: hold, undercut the station, dump into a standing buy order, or reprocess it and sell the materials, each net of the fee that exit actually pays, plus the trade hubs bidding more and how many jumps away they are.

build.question: Is this blueprint worth building today?
build.answer: A Build Plan costs the materials, total job cost and taxes at live hub prices and answers two different questions instead of blurring them: is it cheaper than buying outright, and does it still profit once sales tax and broker fees come off. Sub-builds recurse into the same plan, owned stock is checked against what it would fetch if you sold it instead, and every figure on screen opens the rule it came from with your own values substituted in.

training.question: What is this training plan really going to cost me?
training.answer: Drag skills into a plan and it schedules against the character’s real attributes, implants and queue. The optimizer places remaps for you — or at markers you drop yourself — and re-costs the plan under what-if implants and an accelerator before you spend anything. Put your characters side by side to see which of them should be training it.

colonies.question: Are my colonies earning what they could?
colonies.answer: The PI Advisor reads every colony and lists what is not working — idle facilities, storage that fills before you are back — then prices what is being left on the table: the ISK/hr you would add by tuning what is already built, and, as a separate figure, by rebuilding from scratch. Every rate is net of export customs and sales tax at your own Accounting level.

appraisal.question: What is this pile of loot actually worth?
appraisal.answer: Paste straight from your inventory, a multibuy or a fitting. The appraisal prices it at the trade hub you pick three ways — sold into buy orders now or listed one step under the cheapest seller, each net of the sales tax and broker fee that route pays, and reprocessed with your own skills. Copy a ready-made sell list, or share the result as a link.

skills.desc: Drag-and-drop skill plans, a remap-, implant- and accelerator-aware optimizer, live queue import, ship mastery and fit checks, and a side-by-side character comparison.

clones.desc: Jump clones, fitted implants and the attributes your training time is actually running on.

industry.name: Industry
industry.desc: Build plans for manufacturing and reactions: materials, total job costs, facility rigs and taxes at live hub prices. A production log tracks what each run really made, Opportunities ranks the blueprints you own and scans the market for what is profitable to build, and BPC Search covers every public blueprint-copy contract by ME/TE, runs, price and jumps.

ships.desc: Build a Fitting against a ship's actual skills and implants, with DPS, tank and cap against a target profile you set, save it to My Fittings with a share code, and compare fits side by side. miningTax.desc: Your output, ISK/hr and raw-vs-refined value over time, plus a tax ledger for moons you mine in someone else’s space: each day’s ore in each system assigned to the payee you owe, tax and ISK snapshotted at assignment, splits, settle-up and payment matching.

planetary.desc: Colonies, extraction timers and idle warnings, a chain planner that fits pins against CPU and powergrid, and an advisor that shows what each colony could earn by tuning or rebuilding it.

market.name: Market
market.desc: Order books for any region or all of them, filtered by jump range and security, with price history, side-by-side compare, price alerts, an appraisal of pasted items or fits net of fees, and Hauling Opportunities ranking routes by expected profit. Built on public price data, so it works whatever you did or didn't grant.

piMap.boardLabel: Planet map: planet types, then raw, processed, refined, specialized and advanced products
piMap.planetsInfo: A colony sits on one planet, and each planet type has its own raw resources. Ticked means you have one (read from your colonies). Click a type you have to hide or show it; click one you don't have to see what it would unlock and where to find one.

0.name: Raw
0.info: Raw resources come out of the ground through extractors. Extractors run for a time you choose and must be restarted when they stop. Other tools call these P0.

1.name: Processed
1.info: A basic factory turns one raw resource into a processed product. Other tools call these P1.

2.name: Refined
2.info: An advanced factory combines processed products. If one planet type yields both raws, it is a one-planet setup with no hauling between planets. Other tools call these P2.

3.name: Specialized
3.info: Specialized products are made from refined ones and usually need goods from several planets. Other tools call these P3.

4.name: Advanced
4.info: Advanced products need a High-Tech Production Plant, which fits only on Barren or Temperate planets, and long chains over many planets. Other tools call these P4.

explainer.title: New to PI? The 60-second explainer
explainer.intro: Planetary Industry (PI) means building a small base on a planet that mines resources and turns them into products you sell. Set it up once; it keeps running while you're offline.
explainer.planetBody: Each planet type holds different raw resources.
explainer.rawBody: Ionic Solutions, pulled out of a Gas planet by an extractor.
explainer.processedBody: A basic factory turns 3,000 Ionic Solutions into 20 Electrolytes.
explainer.refinedBody: An advanced factory combines Electrolytes + Water into Coolant.
explainer.commandCenterBody: Your base. Its upgrade level (0–5) gives more room for buildings.
explainer.extractorBody: Drills one raw resource. It runs for a time you choose, then you reset it (every few days).
explainer.factoryBody: Basic factories make processed products from raw. Advanced factories combine two products.
explainer.launchpadBody: Storage that sends products up to the customs office.
explainer.customsBody: The station in orbit where you pick up your products. Its owner keeps a tax.
explainer.skyhookBody: A sovereignty structure some nullsec planets have next to the customs office. It isn't part of your colony; ignore it for PI.
explainer.onePlanet: A one-planet setup does everything on one planet: extractors → basic factories → (advanced factory). No hauling between planets.

columns.hubFromTip: The trade hub each item is bought at: the other hub with the best price gap to your destination.

columns.expectedTip: Expected sell price: what you should get per unit if you list to sell. The lower of one tick under the cheapest listing and what it recently sold for. Click a row to see how.
columns.marginTip: Profit as a percentage of what the load costs, after the sales tax and broker fee on the sale. Open a row for the full working.
columns.daysTip: How long the units listed within 1% of your price, plus about a day's worth of yours, take to sell at the recent sales rate. The mark shows how steadily it trades: a filled dot most days, a ring in bursts, a square rarely.

columns.marginInstantTip: Profit as a percentage of what the load costs, after the sales tax on the sale. Nothing is listed, so there is no broker fee. Open a row for the full working.

a.delete: Settings › Data & storage › Delete all data deletes every character's synced data from our server, then erases everything on this device. Another device still logged in keeps its own copy and can sync it back. Log out of all characters clears this device only.
a.update: The app updates itself in the background. To get a new version now, open Settings › Data & storage and press Update now: it checks and reloads.
a.pushKinds: Only alerts whose time is known ahead: a skill level finishing, training stopping or a queue ending, an industry job finishing, a courier delivery due, a clone jump ready, a PI extraction finishing or an extractor expiring, a calendar event starting, a structure low on fuel, and EVE timers such as a reinforcement ending. Everything else needs the app open. Turn them on in Settings › Notifications.
